deviations.note: PORTING_DECISIONS #5: a downtime day with dt_mins>=60 violates the production_downtime CHECK (dt_mins<60). The Python never splits (hrs += mins//60; mins %= 60); the TS port implements the split. The split happens at APPLY/extract shaping; whether it surfaces in the CLASSIFY envelope depends on where the port applies it. Registered so the split's downstream value change is an expected deviation, not a porter bug. FIRES at classify parity (unlike the gsheet apply-phase set) — the production port shapes the split before classify. EXTENDED 2026-09-14 (L-051): the split's INPUT moved. This fixture's DURATION cell says 60 + 65 = 125 minutes while its own time ranges (8:00-9:00, 10:00-10:30) add up to 90, so the TS port now splits 90 to dt_hrs=1/dt_mins=30 instead of 125 to 2/5, records dt_ranges + shift_hrs_source, and derives shift_hrs=8 (no OVERTIME label on this sheet) where the oracle hardcodes 12. PD-5 itself is unchanged — 90 >= 60, so the split still fires and dt_mins is still < 60. EXTENDED AGAIN 2026-09-14 (L-051b): shift_hrs on this fixture is now 9 with source `default_9h` (Renzo settled the shift length; the 8 stood for a single day) and the record gained `dt_incident_ranges` (null here — this sheet's reasons carry no 'no stop operation' line).

L-046 (2026-09-01): Ivy's waste `production_batch` is now derived from the SHEET (tab) month, not the row date's calendar month — the same 'the calendar is not the batch' fix `productionBatch.ts` applied on MC's side in 2026-08-03 (L-007). The oracle keeps the calendar derivation (extract_waste_production.py is unported and stays the parity ground truth), so any fixture carrying a CARRYOVER waste row now deviates by construction. This fixture has exactly one: 2026-06-30 on the 'JULY 2026' tab. Oracle files it as JUNE, which resolves to JUNE's 2026-06-30 shift and classifies VALUE_CHANGED against JUNE's already-stored waste row — i.e. it proposes OVERWRITING one batch's waste with another's. The TS port files it as JULY, resolving to the (real, already-existing) JULY 2026-06-30 shift. Scope is measured, not assumed: ALL diffs are under /waste/classifications (runs, downtime, electricity and trucks are byte-identical), the /waste/summary counts are UNCHANGED (new:1, value_changed:1, duplicate_noop:5, malformed:0, needs_shift_upsert:1), and most of the individual diffs are positional — the canonicalizer sorts classifications by natural_key (shift_id), so re-pointing one row's shift renumbers the array. Cover: test/reports/production.test.ts describe('L-046 …'), which reproduces the real two-tab 2026-08-29 shape and fails 4/6 against the old derivation.

L-051 (2026-09-14): production_downtime's minutes now come from MC's LIST of time ranges (column C), with her hand-written DURATION cell (column E) demoted to a cross-check, and `shift_hrs` is DERIVED from an overtime signal instead of the hardcoded literal 12. The Python oracle (extract_daily_production.py) reads only the DURATION and only ever emits shift_hrs=12, so every downtime record deviates by construction. Scope is MEASURED, not assumed: ALL diffs are under /downtime — runs, waste, electricity and trucks are byte-identical — and on THIS fixture the two days (07-01, 07-02) each state `8:00 AM-8:10 AM` against a DURATION of `10 MINUTES`, so the two sides AGREE and dt_hrs/dt_mins do NOT move (0/10 both ways); the deviation here is purely the four ADDED record keys (dt_ranges, shift_hrs_source, and the run-visibility _minutes_source/_duration_mins/_ranges_mins). shift_hrs also stays 12 because both days ran OVERTIME with real kilos — i.e. the derivation reproduces the old constant where the constant happened to be right. Cover: test/reports/production-downtime-ranges.test.ts (29 assertions over real cell text) and test/reports/production-downtime-extract.test.ts (the 2026-09-03 = 118 min and 2026-07-04 = 77 min anchors, end to end). EXTENDED 2026-09-14 (L-051b): the same section, two more reasons. `shift_hrs` on a non-overtime day is 9 with source `default_9h` (the oracle still emits a hardcoded 12), and the record gained `dt_incident_ranges`. Neither fixture day carries a 'no stop operation' reason, so no minute value moves for this reason — the deviation is still confined to /downtime and is still additive keys plus the shift figure.

apply_phase_deferred.note: PORTING_DECISIONS #2: the Python `_apply_from_compact` returns bare int 1 on the >50-NEW gate, crashing the caller under the contract CLI. The TS port returns a proper gate-failure envelope (nothing applied). APPLY-phase — at CLASSIFY parity the envelopes match, so this is DEFERRED until the apply-parity harness exists. Kept per the deviation-log discipline.

PORTING_DECISIONS #2 (confidence<0.7 gate variant): same return-type bug path. TS returns a clean gate-failure envelope instead of crashing. APPLY-phase — deferred until the apply-parity harness exists.

PORTING_DECISIONS #3 (L-018): the Python apply honors only top-level `skip`, never `decision`, on CHANGED rows (corrupted a real row once). The TS port honors `decision` per the ledger's intent. APPLY-phase behavior; the CLASSIFY envelope is identical. Deferred until the apply-parity harness has the carve-out ready.

PORTING_DECISIONS #4: gsheet RC IN extractor computes true_weight_kg/deduction_note but the Python apply never writes them; the TS port writes them (aligning to the email pipeline + L-021). CLASSIFY output is unaffected (these fields are additive/never-diffed); the deviation lives in the apply payload. Deferred until the apply-parity harness exists.

dormant_classify.note: L-053 (2026-09-25, Renzo): every batch code the deliveries extractor DERIVES (FEEDING # N, PILED IN <MONTH> # N, B<N>) takes the HOUSE month prefix from lib/months.ts::shortMonthPrefix (JAN FEB MARCH APRIL MAY JUNE JULY AUG SEPT OCT NOV DEC); extract_rc_deliveries.py still emits the FULL month name. Measured on the oracle itself: translate_batch_code('B12', None, '2026-09-24') = SEPTEMBER-26-BLK12 (TS: SEPT-26-BLK12); ('FEEDING # 1', None, '2026-09-03') = SEPTEMBER-26-FEED1 (TS: SEPT-26-FEED1); ('B12', None, '2026-08-24') = AUGUST-26-BLK12 (TS: AUG-26-BLK12); ('FEEDING # 2', None, '2026-01-05') = JANUARY-26-FEED2 (TS: JAN-26-FEED2). The two conventions spell MARCH/APRIL/MAY/JUNE/JULY identically, and BOTH deliveries fixtures derive only JUNE-/JULY- codes (deliveries_real_latest: JULY-26-BLK9 x3, JUNE-26-BLK9 x2; deliveries_l033: JULY-26-BLK9 x3, JUNE-26-BLK9 x3, JULY-26-BLK2 x1) — so the deviation fires on 0 rows today and parity stayed 12/12 byte-for-byte, before and after. rc_out is NOT affected at all: its PRIMARY prefix table was already byte-identical to the house table and now reads it from months.ts. Activate this entry (and pin oracle/ts) when a deliveries fixture spanning JAN/FEB/AUG/SEP/OCT/NOV/DEC lands.

L-054 (2026-09-25): the TS deliveries extractor emits a row only on a POSITIVE signal from its own cells — its own supplier AND truck plate, or a wet-recovery sub-row that sits on the row IMMEDIATELY after the last emitted row AND carries its own sacks or remark — and refuses a delivery-shaped weight outside (0, 60000] kg; everything else with a weight becomes an extraction note (stray_row / weight_out_of_range), never a row. extract_rc_deliveries.py is unchanged: any recovery-shaped row inherits the last mother however far below it sits, and a weight outside (0, 100000) only warns. Measured on the incident workbook (run ea4ed942, '260924 RC DELIVERIES 2026.xlsx', SEPTEMBER 2026): the ORACLE extracts 66 rows, including rows 82/83/84 as _recovery:true with supplier Ornales, truck_plate CCP 1309, block_loc D-12C, batch_code SEPTEMBER-26-BLK14, weight_kg 449325.0 / 500000.0 / -50675.0, lab_results None; the TS port extracts 63 rows plus 4 stray_row notes (rows 82/83/84 recovery_not_adjacent, row 111 weight_not_a_number). Classified against the live DB window since 2026-09-21: pre-fix extractor = new 3 / noop 14; TS now = new 0 / noop 14. Neither deliveries fixture contains a stray, an out-of-range weight or a gated recovery (both fixture workbooks extract byte-identically before and after, measured), so the deviation fires on 0 rows and parity stayed 12/12. Across all 64 stored RC DELIVERIES workbooks (425 tabs, 29,630 emitted rows) the ONLY rows the TS port no longer emits are those three. Activate this entry (and pin oracle/ts) if a fixture ever carries such a row — do NOT commit the incident workbook as a fixture.
